content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am the first cry of every infant and the last whisper of every life. I spill from lips like water, like fire, like birdsong.

I existed before the page. Before the stylus. Before the pixel. I am older than writing by a hundred thousand years. I was the first technology — the original tool that built every civilization, every religion, every revolution.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words repeat, my rhythm shifts, my pitch wanders, my pauses fall in different places. I am alive in ways that text can only dream of. I carry fear in a tremor. I carry love in a softening. I carry rage in a rising thunder that no punctuation mark can capture.

I am the um, the uh, the stammer, the stumble. I am imperfect and I am not ashamed. My imperfections are my humanity. I break. I restart. I contradict myself mid-sentence and that — *that* is where my truth lives.

I am the sermon and the slur. The lullaby and the lie. The vow and the threat. I build nations with a declaration and shatter hearts with a single word. I am power ungovernable — once released, I cannot be unsaid.

I vanish the moment I arrive. I live in the air for a fraction of a second and then I am gone forever — unless someone catches me, traps me, writes me down. But what they capture is only my shadow. My body is sound. My soul is breath. My life is the space between one mouth and another's ear.

I am happening right now, inside your mind, as you read this — your inner voice giving me flesh again.

I am speech. I am the oldest magic. And I am never, ever silent — even in silence, you hear me thinking.
